regulation.framework: MiCA — Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 on Markets in Crypto-Assets
regulation.self_custody_note: ESMA confirms the restriction binds licensed CASP venues, not the asset: individuals may keep holding, sending and withdrawing non-authorized stablecoins to self-custody; decentralized trading sits outside the MiCA services perimeter. USDT is not banned in Europe — it is unavailable on regulated European order books.

USDT.name: Tether USDt
USDT.issuer_note: Tether never applied for MiCA e-money-token (EMT) authorization; its CEO called the significant-token requirement (~60% of reserves held as EU bank deposits) incompatible with its US-Treasury reserve model. Tether also discontinued its euro stablecoin EURT in 2024.

EEA.wave_note: EEA spot pairs disappeared in waves before the hard cliff: Coinbase 2024-12, Crypto.com 2025-01, Binance/Kraken/OKX and the remaining CASPs by 2025-03-31 (ESMA's 'no trace, not even sell-only' deadline). Revolut was the last major platform, with buy ending 2026-07-06 and residual balances auto-converted to fiat after 2026-08-31.
EEA.custody_withdrawal: Most delisting venues retained custody plus on-chain deposit/withdrawal and a convert-to-USDC/EUR/fiat path during wind-down; OKX initially froze USDT sent to EEA accounts by mistake and later enabled on-chain withdrawal. Binance guaranteed continued withdrawals after its own EEA exit. Policies change per venue — verify before sending.
EEA.note: After 2026-07-01 no MiCA-licensed venue can offer USDT trading to EEA residents without risking its CASP licence. Globally USDT remains the dominant stablecoin (~$180bn+) and trades normally in the US, UK, APAC and LatAm; the split is regulatory, not a failure of the token.

USDC.name: USD Coin
USDC.issuer: Circle Internet Financial (EU entity licensed as EMI in France)
USDC.authorized_note: First major stablecoin issuer to receive full MiCA authorization (July 2024), passportable across all member states; the default dollar rail on EEA venues.

EURC.name: Euro Coin
EURC.authorized_note: Circle's euro EMT under the same French MiCA authorization; the regulated euro alternative on most EEA venues.

EURI.name: Eurite
EURI.authorized_note: MiCA-authorized euro e-money token; listed on venues including Bitvavo and (during the Binance wind-down) retained by Binance as an EEA-compliant alternative.

EURCV.name: EUR CoinVertible
EURCV.authorized_note: MiCA-compliant institutional euro EMT; among the few digital assets BISON lists (USDC/USDT deliberately excluded), also on Bitstamp.

USDQ.name: Quantoz USDQ
USDQ.authorized_note: MiCA-authorized dollar stablecoin; together with EURQ it became the primary USD quote rail on Bybit EU after USDT became unavailable.

EURQ.name: Quantoz EURQ
EURQ.authorized_note: MiCA-authorized euro stablecoin; together with USDQ it became the primary quote rail on Bybit EU after USDT became unavailable.

USDT.note: Delisted USDT plus eight other non-MiCA stablecoins (incl. DAI, FDUSD, TUSD) from EEA spot pairs on 2025-03-31; custody, on-chain deposit/withdrawal and Binance Convert to USDC/EURI/EUR remained. Binance withdrew its Greek CASP application on 2026-06-24 and ceased all EEA services at the 2026-07-01 cliff; existing balances remain withdrawable.
First major venue to remove USDT for EEA users (December 2024); EEA order books quote EUR and USDC instead.
Moved EEA users to a sell-only window in March 2025 and ended USDT spot access as the MiCA deadline approached; USDC and EUR pairs remain.

OKX Europe (MFSA Malta) cannot list USDT under MiCA; EEA access removed in the March 2025 wave. USDT sent to EEA accounts by mistake was initially frozen, then an on-chain withdrawal path was enabled.
USDT has never been an EU on-exchange order-book pair at Bitstamp; regulated EU clients use USD/USDC and EUR rails (EURCV also listed).
USDT discontinued for EEA clients during the 2025 MiCA stablecoin wave; USDC and EURC remain, and BTC/USDC (not BTC/USDT) is the dollar-stablecoin band the v0.44 fee model prices.
Announced the USDT delisting in January 2025, ahead of ESMA's 2025-03-31 deadline; now lists the broadest compliant stablecoin set (USDC, EURC, EURI).
Gate's EU entity (Gate Technology, MFSA Malta CASP) removed USDT pairs for EEA residents in the March 2025 wave; the global gate.com USDT books remain reachable only outside the EEA.
EEA residents are restricted to Bybit EU GmbH (FMA Austria), which never listed USDT; its dollar/euro quote rails run on the MiCA-authorized Quantoz USDQ and EURQ stablecoins.
Finst's 400+ markets are EUR and USDC only; USDT was never listed on the platform.

Official BISON support: stablecoins such as USDC and USDT (Tether) are not available and there are no plans to add them; the curated 56-asset list includes the compliant EUR CoinVertible (EURCV) instead.
Non-custodial DEX with USDC collateral and USDC-margined perpetuals only; USDT has never been a collateral or quote asset, and the protocol operates outside the CASP venue perimeter.

No MiCA CASP authorization: the venue itself is region-blocked for every EEA resident since the 2026-07-01 cliff, so its global USDT books cannot be accessed legally from the EEA. USDT trading continues on the global platform for non-EEA users.
